decision: incoming lines are parsed by lanhub-protocol json.rs, a JSON.parse port, not serde_json; a string with a lone surrogate is kept as UTF-16 and written back as \udXXXX
why: serde_json refuses a lone surrogate in a String and would drop the whole line, which the Node hub accepts (slice(0,60) of a name or slice(0,200) of a status can cut a pair); handlers also need the JavaScript coercions (String(), Number(), truthiness) on wrongly typed fields
evidence: a raw transcript of about 230 lines with lone surrogates and odd types is byte-identical to the Node hub apart from the intended cuts: scratchpad/A2/evidence/transcript-diff.txt
result: kept; nesting deeper than 128 is refused (V8 has no limit), and a path holding a lone surrogate counts as invalid (lanhub paths are Rust strings)

decision: outgoing messages are the typed serde enums of lanhub-protocol; strings that may hold a lone surrogate (JsStr) and numbers echoed from clients (JsNumber, Json) serialize through RawValue in the JSON.stringify form
why: byte parity for text, op inserts, seq and presence.line (1e+21, 1.5)
evidence: lanhub-protocol/tests/shape.rs and the transcript diff
